title: Strange lights while driving in remote TN during FAA groundstop, realized that night my dashcam caught it
excerpt: Last Friday (11/13) I was driving back to deer camp in a remote part of Tennessee. My brother and I were on a high road that had been clearcut, so there were no trees in our immediate line of sight. As we came around a curve, I noticed a strange looking light. Just brighter like Jupiter, but...
content:
Hi. Two quick thoughts...

1. Lots of planes and helicopters and stuff remained in the air during the ground stop. Planes in route continued on their way, for the most part. (While watching traffic into CLT just to see what was going on locally during the stop, I noted a few planes that were diverted to here, but I do not kn ow if that was in any way related to the stop.) It was not like the 9/11 thing, where they ordered all planes in flight to ground and left the skies essentially empty. Other than military traffic -- which would also have been flying during this one.

2. That would mean fewer drones in the park, but not necessarily no drones in the park. People do not always follow such regulations.

FWIW, I wonder if we're looking at something astronomical. To the East

I don't see where you mention the time, which could help pinpoint what might be in the sky. But in general, there were potentially several bright objects in that direction. Including the brightest star in the sky!

Flashing would not be unusual, and would be more common for objects closer to the horizon -- scintillation it's called, origin of the famous "Twinkle, twinkle little star!" I can't tell from the video, but movement seems to be largely or entirely a case of the car turning to follow the road.

I'm not insisting that's what it is, but I wonder if that's at least some of it?
